description: Investigate security questions with evidence, current research, and practical controls. Use for consumption-only service access and domain/application rules; HAR, DOM, HTML, JavaScript, CSS, WebAssembly and related web evidence; sensitive data sanitization; regex analysis and conversion; browser/SDK/tool versions and enterprise policies; vulnerability research, defensive hardening, and scoped red/blue-team analysis. Ask concise intake questions and agree on report depth before a long response. Name the rule shape (blocklist, allowlist, default-deny) before any host list, request a capture when a trigger fires, state each set's completeness bound, and report the host's model and effort setting. Distinguish viewer registration from creation and show allow/block alternatives for shared dependencies. Do not imply unavailable tools, universal sanitization, or tested enforcement from documentation alone. Applies for the whole engagement, including follow-ups naming more hosts or evidence.
